body.statement: At the optimal dosage, the exact maximum whitened leverage is \[\mu^\star=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom pj\left(\frac{1-u}{u}\right)^j.\]
body.justification: The leverage is the exact concentration scale of the whitened empirical Gram matrix.
body.gap: Generic bounded-design analyses use dimension-dependent envelopes and do not compute this supply-sensitive Boolean leverage.
body.consumer: The expression gives an explicit sample-size diagnostic before running a sparse-supply interaction experiment.
body.proof_tex:
For an interior dosage, use the triangular matrix \(A\) and the standardized products \(\psi_T\) constructed in the proof of the trace identity. Since \(\Sigma_k(d)^{-1}=A^{\mathsf T}A\) and \(A\phi(x)=\psi(x)\),
\[
 \phi(x)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_k(d)^{-1}\phi(x)
 =\sum_{T\in\mathcal I_k}\psi_T(x)^2.
\]
For a single coordinate,
\[
 \left(\frac{x_i-(2d_i-1)}{\sqrt{4d_i(1-d_i)}}\right)^2
 =\begin{cases}
 (1-d_i)/d_i,&x_i=1,\\
 d_i/(1-d_i),&x_i=-1.
 \end{cases}
\]
At \(d=d^\star\), one has \(0<u\le1/2\), so every nonnegative factor in every subset product is simultaneously maximized by taking \(x_i=1\) for all \(i\). The maximum is therefore
\[
 \mu^\star
 =\sum_{T\in\mathcal I_k}\prod_{i\in T}\frac{1-u}{u}
 =\sum_{j=0}^k\binom pj\left(\frac{1-u}{u}\right)^j.
\]
All support points have positive probability because \(0<u<1\), so this algebraic maximum is also the essential maximum needed below.
